clues.kinetics: The suspension delivers the same total drug to the circulation as the tablets, only absorbed somewhat faster. It is 76% bound to plasma proteins, and 72% of a dose is excreted in urine, mostly as metabolites.
clues.substance: The active moiety has a molecular weight of 236.27 and is a white to off-white powder, practically insoluble in water but soluble in alcohol and acetone.
clues.product: Approved under an NDA as a 100 mg per 5 mL oral suspension.
clues.safety: Boxed warning for serious skin reactions linked to the HLA-B*1502 allele. Contraindicated after bone marrow depression or tricyclic sensitivity; dizziness and drowsiness are common.
clues.indication: Epilepsy, including partial seizures and generalized tonic-clonic seizures, and the pain of true trigeminal neuralgia.
clues.mechanism: The mechanism is unknown; it appears to reduce polysynaptic responses and block post-tetanic potentiation, and it is chemically unrelated to other drugs of its use.

tell: An anticonvulsant that induces its own metabolism, so its half-life falls from 25 to 65 hours to 12 to 17 hours over weeks of dosing.

evidence.pk.tmaxH: plasma levels peak at approximately 1.5 hours
evidence.pk.halfLifeH: decreasing to 12 to 17 hours on repeated doses
